patterns.title: Progressive layer reveal
patterns.definition: Never show a full architecture at once. Build it one layer at a time, in data-flow order:
patterns.text:
Never show a full architecture at once. Build it one layer at a time, in data-flow order:

```
Sources  →  Integration / ETL  →  Storage  →  Analytics  →  Consumers
```

Each layer fades up only after the previous one has done something visible. Used for: DataCube, the Mobile Money platform, the capstone, the RAG pipeline, the HTTP path.
patterns.diagram: Sources  →  Integration / ETL  →  Storage  →  Analytics  →  Consumers

patterns.title: Step transport
patterns.definition: Any process with an order gets play / pause / next / back / reset / speed, visible on screen as a transport bar, with a step counter (`stage 4 / 9`). The current state stays on screen at every step; the viewer must never have to remember the previous frame.
patterns.text:
Any process with an order gets **play / pause / next / back / reset / speed**, visible on screen as a transport bar, with a step counter (`stage 4 / 9`). The current state stays on screen at every step; the viewer must never have to remember the previous frame.
Used for: sorting, BFS/DFS, SQL logical execution, MapReduce, Spark stages, Kafka consumption, RAG retrieval, the agent loop, the Transformer.

patterns.title: State made visible
patterns.definition: Anything internal that controls behaviour is drawn beside the thing it controls, not described:
patterns.text:
Anything internal that controls behaviour is **drawn beside the thing it controls**, not described:
stack · heap · call frames · queue · frontier · visited set · offset pointer · partition boundary · connection pool occupancy · retry budget · lock table · residual stream · context-window budget · cache · filter context.
Rule: never say "the offset advanced". Show a marker moving along a log.
rules: never say "the offset advanced". Show a marker moving along a log.

patterns.title: Live parameter experiment
patterns.definition: One control changes one number; the picture redraws immediately and the outcome is measured on screen.
patterns.text:
One control changes one number; the picture redraws immediately and the outcome is measured on screen.
learning rate · k in kNN · chunk size · pool size · Spark partition count · arrival rate · temperature · top-p · isolation level · replication factor · retention days · sample size.
Rule: **every parameter change must produce a visible consequence within 400 ms.**
rules: every parameter change must produce a visible consequence within 400 ms.

patterns.title: Before / after split screen
patterns.text:
| Left | Right |
|---|---|
| spreadsheet filter | SQL `WHERE` |
| full table scan | index seek |
| normalized | denormalized |
| healthy pipeline | failed pipeline |
| raw export | cleaned export |
| unsafe agent | guarded agent |
| cold connection | warm connection |
| one partition | balanced partitions |

patterns.title: Data moving on edges
patterns.definition: Dots, packets or marching dashed lines travel along the arrows. Used everywhere data physically moves: ETL, HTTP, Kafka events, HDFS block replication, Spark shuffle, JDBC round trips, retrieval, tool calls.
patterns.text:
Dots, packets or marching dashed lines travel along the arrows. Used everywhere data physically moves: ETL, HTTP, Kafka events, HDFS block replication, Spark shuffle, JDBC round trips, retrieval, tool calls.
Rule: **an arrow that never carries a moving mark is decoration — delete it or animate it.**

patterns.title: Matrix / heatmap
patterns.definition: Grid with per-cell colour intensity. Used for: table data, attention scores, embeddings, confusion matrix, correlation, data-quality grids, the residual stream.
patterns.text: Grid with per-cell colour intensity. Used for: table data, attention scores, embeddings, confusion matrix, correlation, data-quality grids, the residual stream.

patterns.title: Code trace
patterns.definition: The current source line highlights while variables, stack frames, heap objects and output update beside it. Reference arrows point at identity, not equality — two names pointing at one object share one arrow head.
patterns.text: The current source line highlights while variables, stack frames, heap objects and output update beside it. Reference arrows point at **identity**, not equality — two names pointing at one object share one arrow head.

patterns.title: Terminal simulation
patterns.definition: The command types character by character, then output appears, then the filesystem / process / network state visibly changes. Errors are shown and read, not skipped.
patterns.text: The command types character by character, then output appears, then the filesystem / process / network state visibly changes. Errors are shown and read, not skipped.

patterns.title: Plan and lineage tree
patterns.definition: Query as an operator tree: scan → filter → join → aggregate → sort → output, with row counts flowing upward and fan-out named when rows-out exceeds rows-in. Column lineage draws source column → transformation → result column, and lists separately the columns read but not returned.

Column lineage draws source column → transformation → result column, and lists separately the columns **read but not returned**.

patterns.title: Architecture topology with failure injection
patterns.definition: Components carry capacity, utilisation and health. Then one component is failed on purpose, and the film follows: propagation → retry → timeout → queue build-up → circuit breaker → shed → recovery.
patterns.text: Components carry capacity, utilisation and health. Then one component is failed on purpose, and the film follows: propagation → retry → timeout → queue build-up → circuit breaker → shed → recovery.

patterns.title: Dashboard plus cause-and-effect
patterns.definition: When a metric moves — success rate, p95, lag, freshness, mismatch count, error rate — the cause is visible in the same frame, on the other side of the screen. A dashboard alone is a picture; a dashboard with its cause is a lesson.
patterns.text: When a metric moves — success rate, p95, lag, freshness, mismatch count, error rate — **the cause is visible in the same frame**, on the other side of the screen. A dashboard alone is a picture; a dashboard with its cause is a lesson.

patterns.title: Timeline
patterns.definition: A horizontal time axis with named events. Used for: transaction lifecycle, NRT freshness, SLA windows, test phases, deployment, incident reconstruction, project evolution.
patterns.text: A horizontal time axis with named events. Used for: transaction lifecycle, NRT freshness, SLA windows, test phases, deployment, incident reconstruction, project evolution.

patterns.title: Decision tree
patterns.definition: One question at a time, answered on screen, narrowing to a choice. Used for: picking a store family, batch vs stream, ETL vs ELT, index or not, model family.
patterns.text: One question at a time, answered on screen, narrowing to a choice. Used for: picking a store family, batch vs stream, ETL vs ELT, index or not, model family.

patterns.title: Star schema and cube
patterns.definition: Fact in the centre, dimensions around it. Animate join, slice, dice, drill-down, roll-up. The cube is translucent; slicing removes a plane, dicing selects a sub-cube, drill-down subdivides a cell.

patterns.title: Risk and dependency board
patterns.definition: Kanban cards: risk · dependency · impact · owner · status · mitigation. Used in the D&IM, DR and delivery chapters.

patterns.title: Prediction before reveal
patterns.definition: Before the animation runs, the film asks the viewer one question and pauses on it for 2–3 seconds with a visible beat marker. Then it plays, then it puts expected vs actual side by side. This is the single highest-retention device in the film — use it at least once per act.

patterns.title: Failure-first
patterns.definition: The canonical arc, and the reason this curriculum works:
patterns.text:
The canonical arc, and the reason this curriculum works:

```
looks correct → reveal the hidden defect → trace it → isolate the root cause
   → fix it → re-run the SAME scene → prove recovery
```

Every major mechanism is met **twice**: once working, once broken.

   → fix it → re-run the SAME scene → prove recovery

patterns.title: 3D, only where depth is the point
patterns.definition: Permitted: HDFS block placement and replication, cluster topology, embedding space, the curriculum atlas, CPU↔memory↔disk movement, architecture evolution.
patterns.text:
Permitted: HDFS block placement and replication, cluster topology, embedding space, the curriculum atlas, CPU↔memory↔disk movement, architecture evolution.
Forbidden: definitions, syntax, tables, anything already clearer flat.
**The test:** a 3D shot must *fail* as a static 2D frame before 3D is justified.
rules: a 3D shot must fail as a static 2D frame before 3D is justified.

patterns.title: Callback and zoom-out
patterns.definition: Every act ends by zooming out to the same architecture diagram and lighting up the component the viewer can now explain. The diagram is one asset reused eight times; it is the film's spine made visible.
patterns.text: Every act ends by zooming out to the **same** architecture diagram and lighting up the component the viewer can now explain. The diagram is one asset reused eight times; it is the film's spine made visible.

patterns.title: Row-count funnel
patterns.definition: Beneath any multi-stage data operation, a bar per stage showing how many rows survived it. `14 → 13 → 11 → 2` is a sentence. This single device explains grain, filtering, joins and fan-out better than any prose.
patterns.text: Beneath any multi-stage data operation, a bar per stage showing **how many rows survived it**. `14 → 13 → 11 → 2` is a sentence. This single device explains grain, filtering, joins and fan-out better than any prose.

patterns.title: Cost counter beside every move
patterns.definition: Comparisons, swaps, page reads, network bytes, milliseconds, rows examined — counted on screen as the operation runs, not summarised at the end in a complexity table.
patterns.text: Comparisons, swaps, page reads, network bytes, milliseconds, rows examined — counted on screen as the operation runs, not summarised at the end in a complexity table.
